title: Dual CNF preserves width
statement: Let $\varphi$ be a DNF formula on $n$ variables, that is, a list of terms, each term a list of literals, and let its De Morgan dual CNF be obtained by negating every literal of every term. Then the dual CNF has the same width as $\varphi$, where the width of a formula is the maximum number of literals appearing in any of its terms (equal to $0$ when the formula is empty).
hypotheses_covered: φ is a DNF formula on n variables
replaced:
The dual CNF $\mathrm{dnfToDualCNF}\,\varphi$ has the same width as $\varphi$, since
flipping the sign of each literal leaves the number of literals per term (and hence
per clause) unchanged.
